new_entities.name: Pterostilbene
new_entities.description: A dimethylated stilbene related to resveratrol and marketed for metabolic, longevity, and antioxidant effects.

new_entities.name: Human metabolic markers
new_entities.description: Human metabolic biomarkers including lipids, blood pressure, body composition, glucose, or related laboratory measures.

edges.population: adults with hypercholesterolemia or healthy adults receiving supplemental pterostilbene-containing products
edges.mechanism: Pterostilbene may influence metabolic signaling through pathways related to antioxidant stress responses, lipid handling, and insulin sensitivity. In humans, however, the most direct evidence shows a conflicted profile, with some improvements in blood pressure or minor body-composition signals offset by an increase in LDL cholesterol and many null laboratory findings.
edges.summary: Pterostilbene should be treated as a mixed metabolic edge, not a straightforward metabolic-support supplement. The cleanest placebo-controlled human trial found reduced blood pressure but also an increase in LDL cholesterol, and later human studies have been mostly small, combination-based, or safety-oriented rather than strongly efficacy-driven.
edges.caveats: The clinical evidence is still thin and much of it does not isolate pterostilbene cleanly from co-ingredients. This is exactly the kind of supplement where mechanistic hype has run ahead of reliable human outcome data.
